candidates.lead: Bader Al-Akkad's "long journey" took in the war in Syria and a career-ending cancer diagnosis
candidates.evidence_text: A former footballer whose playing career was cut short by cancer has said co-founding a club in Dubai aimed at "giving people second chances" felt like "a massive achievement" Bader Al-Akkad, from Manchester, had to leave Stockport County's academy side after being diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma in 2021, ending his dreams of a professional contract After being given the all-clear, he started Phoenix United with his brother Amer, 27, to provide both sporting and academic opportunities to those wanting to follow their own footballing dreams "It's been a long journey of building... and to take this step now has been a massive achievement for us," said Bader, who is preparing for the side's first season in the UAE Third Division Bader and Amer were born in Manchester to Syrian parents, but spent their early years in Damascus after his family returned there They left Syria for the UK in 2012, a year after anti-government protests and a violent crackdown had escalated into conflict

candidates.evidence_text: Sixteen-year-old James Conway was working as a milkman when World War Two broke out in the September of 1939 Conway, from Edgeley in Stockport, signed up to join the Royal Marines where he trained for a secret mission, later named Operation Frankton He was among 12 men chosen to be part of what was widely considered to be one of the most audacious raids during the war Conway's story has featured in BBC Radio Manchester's Hidden Manchester series, which shares the forgotten, untold and heroic stories of the region By March 1942, Britain was struggling to fight back against Nazi Germany The mission was to attack enemy German ships, known as blockade runners, moored at the port of Bordeaux in occupied France

candidates.lead: Justine, 45, is urging people to think carefully before using sunbeds following her diagnosis
candidates.evidence_text: A mother-of-three who used sunbeds in her late teens and early 20s has urged people to think carefully before using them after being diagnosed with a skin tumour Justine Robinson, from Bury, Greater Manchester, said she used the tanners "on and off" before holidays or nights out because she wrongly believed she needed a "base tan" "I can't help wondering whether that's what caused this - it just isn't worth it," said the 45-year-old, who is now recovering after skin cancer surgery Her warning comes after a government consultation on proposals to introduce new safeguards using powers under the Sunbeds Act in England Justine discovered she an uncommon type of melanocytic tumour – which means it cannot be classified as either benign or malignant - after she was referred to a specialist at Salford Royal Hospital It was treated as melanoma as a precaution and she was referred to The Christie for a wider local excision to remove additional tissue around the mole

candidates.evidence_text: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away

candidates.lead: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
candidates.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town centre by 2040 Bev Craig, who became metro mayor of Greater Manchester in July, said: "I want to carry on and go further with the work of Mayoral Development Corporations across the region "I want to build genuinely affordable homes on publicly owned land and, by getting the private sector to back us, I'm excited about what we can achieve with our MDCs, in places like Ashton-under-Lyne, Stalybridge and Oldham." Mayoral Development Corporations are used to speed up regeneration projects by bringing land, funding, and planning powers together to attract investment They are able to use compulsory purchase powers to make sites available for housing projects and many MDCs are able to grant planning permission for developments

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Firefighters have brought a fresh wildfire in Greater Manchester under control in an area plagued by the blazes all summer Fire crews were sent to the blaze near Holmfirth Road in Oldham, at about 22:25 BST on Wednesday - with the fire covering an area of about 1,640 by 492ft (500m by 150m) at its height Engines remained at the scene on Thursday afternoon dampening down hotspots and working to prevent the fire from spreading It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Dove Stone Reservoir and Swineshaw for almost three weeks, with a major incident declared The major incident was stood down earlier this month are the fires were largely contained Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said the latest fire was not connected to those earlier blazes and the cause was being investigated

candidates.evidence_text: A mother-of-three who used sunbeds in her late teens and early 20s has urged people to think carefully before using them after being diagnosed with a skin tumour Justine Robinson, from Bury, Greater Manchester, said she used the tanners "on and off" before holidays or nights out because she wrongly believed she needed a "base tan" "I can't help wondering whether that's what caused this - it just isn't worth it," said the 45-year-old, who is now recovering after skin cancer surgery Her warning comes after a government consultation on proposals to introduce new safeguards using powers under the Sunbeds Act in England Justine discovered she an uncommon type of melanocytic tumour – which means it cannot be classified as either benign or malignant - after she was referred to a specialist at Salford Royal Hospital It was treated as melanoma as a precaution and she was referred to The Christie for a wider local excision to remove additional tissue around the mole

candidates.evidence_text: Twenty people have been charged in connection with the large-scale theft of plant hire machinery worth about £1m The 14 men and six women were all arrested in 2025 as part of an investigation by Cheshire Police into the theft of equipment - mainly mechanical diggers - from hire companies across the UK The force previously said the investigation involved an alleged conspiracy spanning from September 2020 to February 2025 The allegations involved using false identities in order to hire out plant equipment "with no intent of ever returning the machines," it added The reported thefts took place in Cheshire, Lancashire, Cumbria, Humberside, Hampshire, West Midlands, Hertfordshire, Somerset, Staffordshire, Merseyside, Derbyshire, Greater Manchester, North Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, Suffolk, Cornwall and Lincolnshire The following suspects are set to appear in Chester Magistrates' Court on 9 September

candidates.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town centre by 2040 Bev Craig, who became metro mayor of Greater Manchester in July, said: "I want to carry on and go further with the work of Mayoral Development Corporations across the region "I want to build genuinely affordable homes on publicly owned land and, by getting the private sector to back us, I'm excited about what we can achieve with our MDCs, in places like Ashton-under-Lyne, Stalybridge and Oldham." Mayoral Development Corporations are used to speed up regeneration projects by bringing land, funding, and planning powers together to attract investment They are able to use compulsory purchase powers to make sites available for housing projects and many MDCs are able to grant planning permission for developments

Maybe it’s the devil we don’t know that we need to go with.” View 6 Images Oldham is known for its divisive politics but News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:41, 16 Aug 2026 Some in Oldham are ready to welcome ‘the devil they don’t know’ after a months-long ‘Mexican stand off’ keeps going around in ‘vicious circles’ At the end of July, Oldham Council officially declared it is breaking the law with the cause of this being an ongoing row over who should be leading the local authority. After three months with no one in charge, things are still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency Last month, the council’s top legal boss Alex Bougatef declared the council was acting unlawfully without anyone in charge issuing what is called a Section 5 Repor t. This sets in motion a process that could see outside intervention if no solution is found at a meeting on August Commissioners are officials sent by the UK Government to help run councils deemed to be failing or breaking the law with little local say. Often brought in when a council goes effectively bankrupt, commissioners being imposed due to an unshifting political quarrel like Oldham's i Some parties think this scenario is unlikely given voters will be going to the polls again next May to elect another third of councillors potentially changing the council's makeup. However if that were to happen, it would come at a cost of at least £1,200 a day

No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

evidence_packet.lead: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space.
evidence_packet.summary: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

The crackdown was launched amid 'persistent' reports of anti-social behaviour, drug-related crime and the exploitation of vulnerable residents on the Thornbank Estate As part of the operation, two closure orders were issued in the area as three further addresses were also closed through 'tenancy action or voluntary surrender'. A new Urban Care and Neighbourhood (UCAN) centre was also opened in the centre of the estate Over the last 15 months, police said the number of incidents reported has halved and crime volume has reduced by almost 30 per cent. Maybe it’s the devil we don’t know that we need to go with.” View 6 Images Oldham is known for its divisive politics but News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:41, 16 Aug 2026 Some in Oldham are ready to welcome ‘the devil they don’t know’ after a months-long ‘Mexican stand off’ keeps going around in ‘vicious circles’ At the end of July, Oldham Council officially declared it is breaking the law with the cause of this being an ongoing row over who should be leading the local authority. After three months with no one in charge, things are still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency Last month, the council’s top legal boss Alex Bougatef declared the council was acting unlawfully without anyone in charge issuing what is called a Section 5 Repor t. This sets in motion a process that could see outside intervention if no solution is found at a meeting on August Commissioners are officials sent by the UK Government to help run councils deemed to be failing or breaking the law with little local say. Often brought in when a council goes effectively bankrupt, commissioners being imposed due to an unshifting political quarrel like Oldham's i Some parties think this scenario is unlikely given voters will be going to the polls again next May to elect another third of councillors potentially changing the council's makeup. However if that were to happen, it would come at a cost of at least £1,200 a day

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-yera-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, brand-new political staffer Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Mancheste The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' Now I look back and think, well, no wonder I had the s**t kicked out of me!"

Stephen Topping reports. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Man wearing Leonardo DiCaprio jumper launches tiles off roof in 40 hour police stand-off The incident first started in Ash Street, Salford, on Thursday evening Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:43, 15 Aug 2026 View A man involved in a 40 hour stand-off with police in Salford has been pictured launching tiles from a roof The man has been on the roof of a building on Ash Street, near the junction with Field Street, since Thursday evening (August 13). Police have remained on the scene since as officers try to negotiate with him This afternoon (Saturday) the man, who is wearing a jumper with Leonardo DiCaprio on, remained on the roof. Pictures, which the M.E.N has chosen to blur, showed him throwing tiles from the building as he refused to come down Firefighters and paramedics were also called to the scene. This morning, pictures showed riot police wearing protective gear on the street A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said officers are working to get the man down 'as soon as possible'. A cordon remains in place as crews work in the area

The crackdown was launched amid 'persistent' reports of anti-social behaviour, drug-related crime and the exploitation of vulnerable residents on the Thornbank Estate As part of the operation, two closure orders were issued in the area as three further addresses were also closed through 'tenancy action or voluntary surrender'. A new Urban Care and Neighbourhood (UCAN) centre was also opened in the centre of the estate Over the last 15 months, police said the number of incidents reported has halved and crime volume has reduced by almost 30 per cent. A police chief said the estate has been 'transformed' during the crackdown The operation, between GMP, Bolton Council and Be One Homes, came to an end this week. Sergeant Oliver Cooper, from GMP's Neighbourhood Team in Bolton said: "This operation has been significant in increasing public confidence and safety

The statement said the business would be named The Wandering Peacock, after Pedro, a ‘famous peacock who used to wander around Blackrod’ The planning document added: “This reflects the intention of creating a business rooted in the local community. A proposal to convert a former stained glass studio on Chorley Road, Blackrod, has been published by Bolton council A planning statement said the venture would be food led, with an alcohol licence and ice cream available to take away. The statement said the business would be named The Wandering Peacock, after Pedro, a ‘famous peacock who used to wander around Blackrod’ The planning document added: “This reflects the intention of creating a business rooted in the local community. I have also been contacted by a local college student who grew up in Blackrod, she has asked to paint a large portrait of Pedro to display inside “The unit has gradually deteriorated over many years as a workshop, and the last 2.5 years it has remained unused and underutilised, despite occupying a highly visible location within the heart of Blackrod.” The wanderings of Pedro the peacock were recorded by locals in Blackrod between 2016 and 2019 with sightings of the beloved creature reported on social media

After three months with no one in charge, things are still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency Last month, the council’s top legal boss Alex Bougatef declared the council was acting unlawfully without anyone in charge issuing what is called a Section 5 Repor t. This sets in motion a process that could see outside intervention if no solution is found at a meeting on August Commissioners are officials sent by the UK Government to help run councils deemed to be failing or breaking the law with little local say. Often brought in when a council goes effectively bankrupt, commissioners being imposed due to an unshifting political quarrel like Oldham's i Some parties think this scenario is unlikely given voters will be going to the polls again next May to elect another third of councillors potentially changing the council's makeup. However if that were to happen, it would come at a cost of at least £1,200 a day

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-yera-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, brand-new political staffer Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Mancheste The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' candidates.evidence_text: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Man wearing Leonardo DiCaprio jumper launches tiles off roof in 40 hour police stand-off The incident first started in Ash Street, Salford, on Thursday evening Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:43, 15 Aug 2026 View A man involved in a 40 hour stand-off with police in Salford has been pictured launching tiles from a roof The man has been on the roof of a building on Ash Street, near the junction with Field Street, since Thursday evening (August 13). Police have remained on the scene since as officers try to negotiate with him This afternoon (Saturday) the man, who is wearing a jumper with Leonardo DiCaprio on, remained on the roof. Pictures, which the M.E.N has chosen to blur, showed him throwing tiles from the building as he refused to come down Firefighters and paramedics were also called to the scene. This morning, pictures showed riot police wearing protective gear on the street A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said officers are working to get the man down 'as soon as possible'. A cordon remains in place as crews work in the area

But now, as NHS treatment options dwindle, Sarah has turned to fundraising for private care Sarah said: “It blew our world apart,” recalling her diagnosis in 2019 She added: “I’ve lived with it now for seven years. I’m eternally grateful to The Christie, but we’ve come to a point now where they can’t offer me anything else under the NHS. My team are as frustrated as I am.” Sarah believes the drug Enhertu could help her, but while it is available to NHS patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer in Scotland, it is not yet offered in England

My army is much bigger considering I have Russian and Chinese support. We will be armed and shoot to kill.”

candidates.evidence_text: People living in Manchester have had their lives transformed for the better after accessing voluntary-led services which are kept alive through crucial funding The Our Manchester Voluntary and Community Sector (OMVCS) fund invests £16.5 million across three years to support the stability and resilience of several voluntary organisations for communities across the city. The annual budget increased from £2.4m to £5.5m to ensure essential A significant number of applications were received for the 2026–29 round and funding has now been allocated to 80 selected organisations Manchester is home to over 3,800 voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise organisations. Significant work has ensured this funding reaches communities who need it the most such as deprived wards, marginalised communities like disabled people and racially minoritised grou CEO Leah Chikamba-Mulando said she began the Angels of Hope for Women in 2014 because of the number of Black African women she was encountering who lacked confidence to access mainstream services in the UK Based in Gorton, the organisation became an officially registered charity in 2019, supporting women with anything from housing and immigration to benefits and domestic violence cases

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester saw more homes built in the last year (4,766) than all the 32 Greater London boroughs combined (4,261) a report to the Council’s Communities and Equalities Scrutiny Committee heard today (Weds 22 July) The significant achievement marks another record-breaking year as part of the Council’s ambitious housing strategy up to 2032, which also saw more affordable homes built than at any point since the late 1990s with 901 affordable tenure homes completed – of which around half (439) Manchester is also bucking the national trend for affordable housing starts recording an increase of 12% since 2022/23 And the city centre also saw the largest ever delivery of affordable in the city’s history over the last year with 259 completions, helping to diversify the city centre housing market and help more Manchester people have more choice about where they live The Housing Strategy update shows that the city remains on track to meet its target to deliver at least 36,000 homes of all tenures by 2032, including 10,000 social, Council and genuinely affordable homes – 3,000 of which will be in the city centre 13,555 homes have already been delivered since 2022 with more than 7,800 currently under construction, and a further 20,000 homes with planning approval or in the pipeline

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council's Community Safety Service was granted a three-year Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) following repeated offences targeting retailers in Chadderton Athanial Lucas, 30, of no fixed address, appeared before Tameside Magistrates' Court on 29 July charged with three shoplifting offences at Londis in Chadderton Lucas was sentenced to eight weeks in custody, ordered to pay £513 in compensation and made subject to a Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) until 29 July 2029 The three-year CBO was secured by Oldham Council's Community Safety Service, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police. candidates.lead: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET)
candidates.evidence_text: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) The latest Department for Education (DfE) Local Authority Participation and NEET figures for the 2025/26 academic year show that 93.2 per cent of Oldham's 16 and 17-year-olds are participating in education and training, an increase of 2.8 percentage points on the previous year. T At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. This is significantly lower than both the North West average of 5.5% and the England average of 5.8% The figures also highlight Oldham's strong performance, in partnership with the charity Positive Steps, in tracking and supporting young people Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. This is well below the North West average of 1.3 per cent and the England average of 2.4 per cent

evidence_packet.title: Oldham bucks national trend as more young people choose education and training
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET)
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET)
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) The latest Department for Education (DfE) Local Authority Participation and NEET figures for the 2025/26 academic year show that 93.2 per cent of Oldham's 16 and 17-year-olds are participating in education and training, an increase of 2.8 percentage points on the previous year. T At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. This is significantly lower than both the North West average of 5.5% and the England average of 5.8% The figures also highlight Oldham's strong performance, in partnership with the charity Positive Steps, in tracking and supporting young people Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. This is well below the North West average of 1.3 per cent and the England average of 2.4 per cent

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Inhale Me, Exhale You By Kate Partington Tue 2 Jun 10:00 - Mon 28 Sep 22:00 Art Tue 2 Jun - Mon 28 Sep From 10:00 Tue 2 Jun - Mon 28 Sep From 10:00 Arches Windows No booking required Unspoken feelings and moments of desire You can see this artwork in HOME Arches Windows on Whitwo This piece belongs to a wider series called ‘Desire Me.’ It aims to translate unspoken feelings and moments of desire that occur between us The focus is on longing, on reaching out and on instances of hopeful touch that happen in the early stages of a relationship. It seeks to capture the essence of sensations you get in your stomach that are so hard to verbalise, but that we all know and feel.” Kate Partington’s practice explores the subtleties of touch, connection, and the spaces that exist between bodies She is a mixed media artist working across analogue and digital spaces, constructing images that hover between materiality and emotion Her work examines how intimacy can be both tender and elusive, how connection can be felt rather than seen

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

candidates.evidence_text: Second high-profile senior exit for Co-op as chair Debbie White follows group CEO out of the door - Prolific North Skip to content News Steven Gerrard lands TV role ahead of Premier League season News Reach appoints former TikTok and Immediate exec to lead audio and video Brand Burnley loses one shirt sponsor and gains another within hours Second high-profile senior exit for Co-op as chair Debbie White follows group CEO out of the door Brand , Ecommerce by Chris Newbould August 12, 2026 The Co-op Group has confirmed that chair Debbie White is to step down as both chair and member of the board. Moni Mannings, senior independent director, has been appointed interim chair. White’s departure follows a high-profile cyber attack on the Manchester-based retail giant as a string of big high street names were hit by hackers in 2025, as well as the departure of group CEO Shirine Khoury-Haq in March of this year, followed by a hefty bonus payout despite the £285m cyber attack, amid reports of a “toxic work culture” at the top of the organisation. Khoury-Haq denied the claims at the time saying that her decision to leave was “Very much a personal decision.” She added: “The reason is I want to go and do something else,” although the latest seemingly unexpected departure at the top seems unlikely to quell any existing rumours. READ MORE: Online subscriptions in the spotlight as Burnham promises crackdown on “rip off” business practices White joined the group in 2023 and was made chair in 2024, taking over from Allan Leighton. Before that, she held a series of executive and non-executive roles, including group chief executive of Interserve and global CEO for healthcare and government at Sodexo, and senior independent director at Spire Healthcare Group, Howden’s Joinery Group and PAVmed Inc. White said: “It has been a privilege to serve as chair of our Co-op during a period which has brought both opportunity and challenge for our businesses. Despite a variety of headwinds facing our businesses, and the impact of last year’s malicious cyber-attack, it is clear that the actions that we have taken are having a positive impact and will ensure we have the strong foundations to deliver on our vision and strategy.” White added that with the process to appoint a permanent group CEO under way following the departure of Khoury-Haq, it was the “right time to step down as chair”, as she was nearing the end of her first term and “not in a position to commit to a further three-year term … at this time.” The move means she will also be stepping down as chair of the government’s Mutual and Co-operative Sector Business Council She added: “My stepping down will enable this crucial appointment to be made by Moni and fellow board members, who will continue to steer the business through this important period. “My decision has been made easier knowing that our Co-op is back in a position of stability and opportunity. Under the leadership of interim CEO Kate Allum, supported by a highly capable leadership team, board and council, the organisation is well placed to continue building momentum and delivering for its members and customers. “I would like to thank my fellow board members, council members and colleagues across the Co-op for their support, dedication and commitment. I wish Kate, Moni and everyone connected with the Co-op every success for the future. candidates.evidence_text: $7m funding round as Manchester startup addresses cyber risk of growing AI role in software development - Prolific North Skip to content News Steven Gerrard lands TV role ahead of Premier League season News Reach appoints former TikTok and Immediate exec to lead audio and video Brand Burnley loses one shirt sponsor and gains another within hours $7m funding round as Manchester startup addresses cyber risk of growing AI role in software development Tech by Chris Newbould August 12, 2026 Manchester cybersecurity start-up Cytix has announced a $7M (£5m) Series A funding round to accelerate the company’s mission to tackle the problems created by rapid software change – a reality that is becoming a distinct risk for organisations as AI-assisted development, agentic workflows, and continuous delivery lead to an increased volume of AI-generated code. The round has been led by Northern Gritstone , the venture capital and investment firm that focuses on science and tech startups in the North of England, with participation from existing investors, Auriga Cyber Ventures and NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II). Ben Armstrong, CEO of Cytix said: “We chose Northern Gritstone for their conviction in investing in deeptech companies in the North of England with global ambition. Northern Gritstone and Cytix share the belief that software change is becoming a key risk for organisations, and those that build software need a solution that scales with the current pace of development. We’re also grateful to the existing investors that have backed us since the early days and increased their commitment because they’ve seen the thesis play out.” READ MORE: Not just a diversity issue – an economic one: New South Yorkshire taskforce to address female representation in tech The funding will accelerate the roll out of Cytix’s newly launched change risk platform, designed to address the questions raised by rapid software change: Whether security should care about the change, what risk it introduces, and what the required action should be. The platform continuously monitors every software change or update a business makes, analyses and validates the risk of that change, and explains to regulators how that risk was handled. “Software is changing,” explained Armstrong. “AI-assisted development means change now happens at machine speed. Meanwhile, very few security leaders have control over, or understanding of, those changes from a risk perspective. Right now, existing tools can tell you what vulnerabilities you have, but can’t tell you about the risk. We launched Cytix’ change risk management platform to get control of that risk.” The platform sits between a customer’s software development lifecycle (SDLC) where change happens, and their risk, security and compliance functions where the change is evidenced for compliance purposes. It is the control point through which every software change passes: Understanding what change occurred and the associated business risk, deciding the security action, validating the risk, and providing the evidence to show how it was handled. The Series A round will help Cytix reach customers in enterprise and regulated businesses where change governance is a regulatory obligation. Customers can access the platform either directly with Cytix or through its managed service partnerships with NCC Group and KPMG. Duncan Johnson, CEO of Northern Gritstone, said: “The explosion of AI-assisted software development has led to a race to ensure software implementation remains secure. Cytix’s platform aims to help enterprises take a realistic approach, recognising where change carries the most risk whilst allowing businesses to innovate. Northern Gritstone is proud to support another ambitious Manchester-based business in an exciting phase of its growth.” Cytix’s change risk platform is available on general release for customers on 12 August. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

"For this country as well, he's a future captain of this country and of City as well." Guehi was close to joining Liverpool last summer only for a move to fall through at the eleventh hour. Grealish has only recently returned to team training after recovering from a foot injury picked up while on loan at Everton last season. Grealish looks set for an exit this summer and he is unlikely to play any part this weekend having only just returned to training

candidates.summary: GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне! 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне
candidates.lead: Горан Брегович at Indigo at The O2
candidates.practical_angle: Официальная страница должна подтверждать дату, город, площадку и старт продаж.
candidates.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Connecting industry, academia, founders, investors and policymakers, the event will explore the infrastructure, talent and innovation needed to build the next generation of the intelligence economy Featuring keynote speakers, panel discussions, startup showcases and a private leadership dinner, Future Live will examine how the North can lead the next era of compute and innovation 📅 Date: Thursday 17th September 2026 🕒 Time: 10:00-17:30 📍 Location: Campfield Studios 🎟️ Tickets Tickets are limited to maintain audience quality and seniority We're keen to talk to businesses who would like to partner with us for this event, showcasing their brand in a room filled with influential senior leaders, founders, policy makers and more. Packages to suit all budgets At Manchester Digital, we believe in creating an inclusive and diverse community where everyone feels welcome and valued. We are committed to ensuring that all our event attendees have a safe, enjoyable experience that meets their needs

There will then be a 60-second round and more networking Refreshments (pastries and fruit along with tea/coffee) will be provided We are open, inclusive and welcoming, and we celebrate the diversity which makes up our city region. We ask that all delegates and sponsors uphold our professional code at all times. We'll also be taking photos on the day, so please flag to us if you don't want to be featured
